Try reading fmap or fdt from file first With larger flash chip sizes and slow interfaces, looking up the onboard flash for fmap or fdt could take very long time, especially if the onboard flash is not programmed. On the other hand, the file containing the image to be programmed pretty much always contains fmap or fdt. This patch modifies the interface of the search subsystem to pass it a callback function to search the image instead of passing it the flash structure pointer. The search function first is called with the callback to search in the supplied image file, and then if the file was not supplied or neither map nor fdt were not found - try again, this time looking in the chip itself, using a callback which reads in the flash. BRANCH=none BUG=b:79492818 TEST=verified that invoking flashrom with -w and -i, when trying to program a fully erased flash chip, does not hang for a very long time while fmap is searched, as it is retrieved from the supplied file. CHROMIUM: tpm: cr50_spi: fix tpm ready timeouts Modern cr50 builds use "tpm ready" IRQ to signal that cr50 is done processing the previous transaction and is ready for the next one. Old cr50 builds and platforms didn't support this interrupt, so the driver needed to make sure that some delay is made between transactions. cr50_spi still needs to support both old and modern cases. Before this CL, the cr50_spi driver was always waiting for "tpm ready" IRQ with a 2 msec delay. In practice, while performing long internal background operations (like nvmem commit not caused by a command), cr50 may delay processing the transaction by dozens of milliseconds (up to 150 msec was observed). If a new transaction header is sent in such case before the previous transaction is processed, it may be lost. Thus it is more reliable to wait for "tpm ready" IRQ for much longer, if that IRQ is supported. This CL does the following: - Increases the delay between transactions from 2 msec to 10 msec in cases when IRQ is not supported. 10 msec is the value used for this purpose by firmware. - When IRQ is supported, uses TPM2 Timeout A (750 msec) as the timeout while waiting for IRQ. - Adds logic to confirm that IRQs are actually triggered if "tpm ready" IRQ is configured (to protect from old cr50 revisions, which don't trigger it). And switches to the longer timeout only if the IRQ is confirmed. - Adds a warning if IRQ is confirmed, but waiting for it results in a timeout. BUG=b:73351086 TEST=go through reboot test with fizz, verify that 'Timeout during flow control' doesn't happen.
